- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is flat or negative (≤0.3) and price is near support, model tends to overreact; apply mean reversion to forecast by 0.5–1.5% toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates in early days (1–5) when sentiment is positive; reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lag correction to forecast (i.e., shift forecast 1–2 days ahead).
